title: Central Business District Office Refit
summary: A full interior strip-out and rebuild of a 1,400 m² open-plan office floor, delivered across a phased programme so the client's team stayed operational throughout.
scope: New suspended ceiling grid with integrated lighting
Full electrical first and second fix
challenge: The client could not vacate the building. Every noisy or dust-generating activity had to be scheduled outside core business hours, and the live server room had to remain powered without interruption.
solution: We split the floor into four zones and worked a rolling night programme, sealing each zone with temporary dust barriers. The server room was placed on a temporary supply before the main distribution board was replaced, so uptime was never at risk.
outcome: Handed over on programme with zero recorded downtime for the client's operations team.

title: Lekki Private Residence Rewire
summary: Complete replacement of an ageing domestic electrical installation in a five-bedroom residence, brought up to current standards with full circuit separation and surge protection.
scope: New consumer unit with RCBO protection per circuit
Dedicated circuits for HVAC and borehole pump
challenge: The original installation had been extended piecemeal over years, with undocumented circuits buried in the fabric of the building and no reliable earthing arrangement.
solution: We traced and mapped every existing circuit before any work began, producing an as-found schedule. That map let us plan a rewire that reused existing routes where they were safe and abandoned the rest, keeping the making-good works to a minimum.
outcome: The property now has a fully documented, individually protected installation with a complete test certificate pack for the owner's records.

title: Enugu Retail Unit Fit-Out
summary: Shell-to-trading fit-out of a ground-floor retail unit, covering the design concept, joinery, lighting scheme and final finishes.
scope: Bespoke display joinery in oak veneer
Track lighting scheme with warm colour temperature
challenge: The unit had a low floor-to-ceiling height and only one shopfront elevation for natural light, which risked a cramped and dim trading environment.
solution: We kept the ceiling open rather than dropping a grid, painted the exposed services dark so they visually receded, and used a layered lighting scheme to create brightness at merchandise level without lowering the perceived height.
outcome: A trading space that reads as considerably larger and brighter than its floor plate suggests.

title: Asaba Roof Replacement & Waterproofing
summary: Strip and re-cover of a failing long-span aluminium roof over a two-storey commercial building, including full replacement of the rainwater goods.
scope: Strip existing sheets and inspect timber structure
New gutters, downpipes and drainage connections
challenge: Persistent leaks had been patched repeatedly without success. The real fault was not the sheets but the parapet detail, where water was tracking behind the flashing during driven rain.
solution: Rather than simply re-covering, we opened up the parapet junction, installed a proper upstand and membrane detail, and dressed the new flashing over it. The sheet replacement then sat on a junction that could actually shed water.
outcome: No recorded ingress through two full rainy seasons since completion.

title: Port Harcourt Facility Maintenance Contract
summary: An ongoing planned and reactive maintenance contract covering a mixed-use commercial property, moving the client from break-fix callouts to a scheduled regime.
scope: Annual budget forecasting for the client
challenge: The client had no asset register and no maintenance history, so every failure was a surprise and every repair was priced as an emergency.
solution: We started with a full condition survey and built an asset register from scratch. That let us put the highest-risk items on a planned schedule and gave the client, for the first time, a forecastable annual maintenance budget.
outcome: Reactive emergency callouts dropped substantially in the first year as planned interventions caught faults earlier.

title: Abuja Steel Balustrade & Staircase
summary: Design, fabrication and installation of a feature steel staircase and balustrade system for a residential atrium, finished in powder-coated black with a hardwood handrail.
scope: Workshop fabrication of stringer and treads
Hardwood handrail machined and fitted on site
Balustrade infill to current guarding heights
challenge: The atrium opening was out of square by a noticeable margin, which would have shown badly on a staircase with long straight runs.
solution: We surveyed the opening properly before fabricating anything and set the staircase out to a true line, absorbing the discrepancy in the trimmer detail at the head. The finished stair reads dead straight even though the opening is not.
outcome: A feature staircase that sits true in an opening that is not, with no visible packing or scribing.
